injuries.injury: Wagner (knee) will not return to Wednesday's game against the Bucks, C.J. Holmes of the New York Daily News reports.
injuries.detail: Wagner played just four minutes prior to leaving the contest due to left knee soreness. He scored two points (0-1 FG, 0-1 3Pt) after sinking both free throws. Grant Nelson will get more minutes off the Nets' bench for the remainder of the game.

injuries.injury: Traore will be re-evaluated in approximately 8-10 weeks due to a right hamstring strain, Michael Scotto of HoopsHype.com reports.
injuries.detail: Traore had a productive start to his second year in the NBA, though he's now set to miss an extended period after sustaining a hamstring injury in Friday's loss to Orlando. With the 20-year-old point guard sidelined, Egor Demin, Mikel Brown and Keon Ellis are candidates for increased playing time.

injuries.injury: Schroder (hamstring) is out for Wednesday's game the Bulls.
injuries.detail: Schroder remains out indefinitely with a hamstring strain. With Charlotte already eliminated from knockout-round contention in the NBA Cup, it's possible the veteran's point guard's absence extends into mid-December.

injuries.injury: Allen (concussion) has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against Chicago.
injuries.detail: Allen will miss a fourth consecutive contest due to a concussion. With the veteran swingman sidelined, Sion James (thigh), Grant Williams and Royce O'Neale are candidates for increased playing time. Allen's next chance to play will come Saturday against Brooklyn.

injuries.injury: Knueppel (hamstring) was diagnosed with a left hamstring strain Sunday and will be re-evaluated in four weeks.
injuries.detail: Knueppel missed the first eight games of the 2026-27 campaign. He returned for the 114-104 loss to Brooklyn on Wednesday, though he exited the contest after just six minutes of work and didn't return. With Knueppel out of commission for at least a month, Grayson Allen and Sion James are candidates to replace him in the starting lineup, especially with Dennis Schroder (hamstring) sidelined for a minimum of two weeks.

injuries.injury: Kalkbrenner (hip) has been ruled out for Wednesday's matchup with Chicago.
injuries.detail: Kalkbrenner exited Monday's loss to Memphis early with left hip soreness and is now set to miss Wednesday's contest. His next chance to play will come Saturday against the Nets. With the big man sidelined, Hannes Steinbach could see meaningful playing time behind Moussa Diabate.

injuries.injury: Wilson (hand) is expected to miss four to six weeks, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
injuries.detail: The rookie forward went down during Wednesday's loss to the Spurs, and he now needs surgery to repair a fractured right hand. More pressure will likely fall on Josh Giddey going forward, while the likes of Tre Jones and Isaac Okoro will have a chance for added streaming value.

injuries.injury: Smith (illness) is listed as out for Wednesday's game against Charlotte.
injuries.detail: Smith is dealing with a gastrointestinal illness, so he won't suit up Wednesday versus the Hornets. Without him, Nic Claxton will presumably enter the starting lineup. Zach Collins might also be more involved.

injuries.injury: Powell has been diagnosed with a mild right hamstring strain and will be re-evaluated later this week.
injuries.detail: Powell sustained the hamstring injury in Friday's loss to the Wizards and is now set to miss at least the next two contests. With the veteran swingman on the shelf, Isaac Okoro, Buddy Hield, Tre Jones and Patrick Williams are all candidates for increased playing time.

injuries.injury: Nesmith is out for Monday's game against the Thunder due to right foot soreness.
injuries.detail: The swingman is sitting out the second leg of this back-to-back set and is likely facing a short-term absence. Nesmith's absence should get Obi Toppin onto the streaming map in fantasy leagues Monday.

injuries.injury: Head coach Rick Carlise confirmed Sheppard will miss "months" after undergoing surgery to repair a torn meniscus in his left knee, Tony East of Forbes.com reports.
injuries.detail: Sheppard required a full repair and is without a definitive timetable for a return to action. With Tyrese Haliburton (hamstring) expected to miss at least two weeks, Quenton Jackson figures to see a significant uptick in playing time. Two-way player Braden Smith could also see increased action with the parent club.

injuries.injury: Nance exited Monday's game against the Thunder due to a sore right ankle and he will not return, Tony East of Forbes.com reports.
injuries.detail: Nance will have three full days to rest his sore ankle before the Pacers' next game, although with Friday's matchup with the 76ers being the first of a back-to-back set, Nance may need to miss that one as well. Obi Toppin figures to pick up most of Nance's minutes while he's sidelined.

injuries.injury: McConnell (hamstring) was recalled from the G League's Noblesville Boom on Tuesday, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
injuries.detail: After missing Indiana's past two games with left hamstring soreness, McConnell joined the club's G League affiliate for practice Tuesday. The veteran point guard can be considered questionable for Friday's game against Philadelphia until the Pacers provide an update on his progress.

injuries.injury: Haliburton (hamstring) was recalled from the G League's Noblesville Boom on Tuesday, Tony East of Forbes.com reports.
injuries.detail: Haliburton joined the Pacers' G League affiliate for practice Tuesday, taking a significant step forward in his recovery from a left hamstring strain. However, Shams Charania of ESPN reported Friday that the star point guard is expected to miss at least two more weeks, so Haliburton isn't expected to return to game action in the near future.

injuries.injury: Mara (leg) is out for Wednesday's game versus the Timberwolves.
injuries.detail: This will be Mara's third straight game on the inactive list, and for now, he should be considered questionable at best for Saturday's game in Milwaukee. With Jaylin Williams (back) also unavailable, Micah Peavy and Kenrich Williams will help back up Isaiah Hartenstein at the center position.

injuries.injury: Wallace underwent surgery Friday to repair a torn labrum in his left shoulder and will be re-evaluated before the end of the regular season, Clemente Almanza of USA Today reports.
injuries.detail: Wallace is expected to miss most, if not all, of the season. However, there's still a chance he will return late in the campaign after sustaining the shoulder injury in Sunday's win over the Clippers. With Jalen Williams (leg) also set to be re-evaluated before the end of the regular season, Alex Caruso (ankle) should see significant playing time once cleared to return. In the meantime, Jared McCain, Bennett Stirtz and Josh Dix are expected to see increased burn.

injuries.injury: Holmgren underwent a biological treatment Friday to address a small patellar tendon tear and will miss at least 8-10 weeks, Nick Crain of Slam reports.
injuries.detail: This is another massive blow to an Oklahoma City squad that's already set to be without Jalen Williams (leg) and Cason Wallace (shoulder) for most, if not all, of the season. With Holmgren sidelined, Kenrich Williams, Jaylin Williams and Aday Mara are all candidates to see increased playing time. Two-way player Brooks Barnhizer could also see more minutes.

injuries.injury: Williams (ankle) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Pacers, according to the NBA's official injury report.
injuries.detail: Williams remains sidelined following left ankle surgery, with no confirmed return date. His continued absence leaves Oklahoma City without a key offensive contributor, allowing additional opportunities for the Thunder's remaining perimeter players.

injuries.injury: Williams (back) is listed as out for Wednesday's game against Minnesota.
injuries.detail: Williams has only played twice in the Thunder's last 11 games. It's unclear when he will be available to return, though his next opportunity to suit up will come Saturday in Milwaukee. With Aday Mara (shin) also ruled out, Kenrich Williams and Micah Peavy should both see more action versus the Timberwolves.

injuries.injury: Topic (hip) is listed as out for Wednesday's game versus Minnesota.
injuries.detail: Topic has appeared in only three games for the Thunder this season. He's missed the last three contests because of a hip strain, with his next opportunity to suit up coming Saturday in Milwaukee. Without Topic, Bennett Stirtz and Josh Dix could continue to receive more playing time.

injuries.injury: Sorber underwent an arthroscopic knee procedure Tuesday to address inflammation at the patellofemoral joint in his right knee, and he's expected to return to on-court activities in 6-8 weeks, Steve McGehee of News 9 Oklahoma City reports.
injuries.detail: Once Sorber begins on-court work, there will be a ramp-up period before he's cleared for game-time action, so his absence will likely extend well beyond this initial 6-8-week window. Sorber was selected by the Thunder with the No. 15 pick in the 2025 NBA Draft, but he missed his entire rookie season after tearing the ACL in his right knee and has yet to play this season due to right knee issues.

injuries.injury: Castleton totaled five points (2-4 FG, 1-1 3Pt) and four rebounds in seven minutes during Tuesday's 132-116 preseason win over the Cavaliers.
injuries.detail: Castleton squeezed five points and four boards into his brief appearance, including a successful three-point attempt. The reserve center made productive use of his late-game opportunity, though his limited playing time leaves his regular-season role uncertain.

injuries.injury: Head coach Sean Sweeney said Wednesday that Nelson (ankle) has been doing "some on-court stuff," though Sweeney added that the work has been "minimal," Jason Beede of the Orlando Sentinel reports.
injuries.detail: Nelson underwent surgery this offseason to repair a fractured left ankle. It's encouraging to hear that he's made some progress, but the two-way player can still be considered week-to-week moving forward.

injuries.injury: Isaac (knee) is out for Sunday's game against the Wizards.
injuries.detail: Isaac continues to deal with a knee injury that has kept him out of action for the entire 2026-27 season. He should continue to be considered week to week until the Magic offer an update on his recovery process.

injuries.injury: Penda (hamstring) is making progress but remains without a timetable to return to game action, Jason Beede of the Orlando Sentinel reports.
injuries.detail: Penda suffered a partially torn hamstring in the preseason and can still be considered week-to-week moving forward. With the second-year forward and Paolo Banchero (ankle) both sidelined, Tristan da Silva and Jamal Cain should continue seeing increased minutes.

injuries.injury: Banchero is expected to be sidelined for the next four-to-six weeks due to a right high-ankle sprain, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
injuries.detail: Banchero left during Friday's loss against the Timberwolves due to an ankle injury, and follow-up tests have confirmed a high-ankle sprain for the fifth-year forward. With an extended absence expected, the Magic will have to rely more heavily on Franz Wagner and Desmond Bane offensively, and Tristan da Silva figures to be the top candidate to enter the Magic's starting lineup for as long as Banchero is sidelined.

injuries.injury: Hukporti has sustained a season-ending ruptured right Achilles tendon, per Shams Charania of ESPN.
injuries.detail: Hukporti went down with an Achilles injury in Monday's preseason opener against the Knicks, and an MRI has since revealed a rupture. He signed a one-year deal with the 76ers over the summer, so Hukporti will be an unrestricted free agent come season's end. With Hukporti's year already finished, Adem Bona (foot) should assume the backup center role behind Joel Embiid once healthy.

injuries.injury: Brown (hamstring) will receive imaging, and the Sixers will provide an update Thursday, Ky Carlin of USA Today reports.
injuries.detail: Brown will get imaging on his troublesome left hamstring that he reaggravated in the second quarter of Wednesday's 111-104 win over Miami. He recently missed two games with the ailment, and it sounds like he could be in jeopardy of another stint on the sidelines. While Brown is out, Dean Wade is the top candidate to join the starting unit, while Kentavious Caldwell-Pope and Anfernee Simons are likely to see an increase in playing time off the bench.

injuries.injury: Embiid (illness) is out for Wednesday's game against Miami, Ira Winderman of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
injuries.detail: With Embiid set to miss a second straight game due to illness after previously being listed as doubtful, Philadelphia will again need to cover his vacated minutes at center. His absence removes one of the 76ers' top offensive options and should leave added frontcourt work available to the likes of Jabari Walker, Dominick Barlow and Adem Bona.

injuries.injury: The Wizards announced Thursday that Watkins has undergone surgery for a torn ACL.
injuries.detail: Watkins, a two-way player for the Wizards, suffered the injury during the Summer League. Although Washington has yet to offer a timetable for a return, a typical recovery time for the procedure is approximately 9-to-12 months. That leaves Watkins in serious jeopardy of missing most, if not all, of the 2026-27 season, and it remains to be seen if the team will continue keeping him around on a two-way roster spot while he's injured.

injuries.injury: Champagnie (foot) is expected to miss several months, per Josh Robbins of The Athletic.
injuries.detail: The forward underwent surgery Wednesday to address a fractured foot, and the Wizards hope Champagnie will be ready to return at some time around the All-Star break in February. The likes of Bilal Coulibaly, Tre Johnson and Bub Carrington will all be asked to help pick up the slack for the foreseeable future.

injuries.injury: The Wizards announced Monday that Beekman sustained a right acromioclavicular joint injury and will be re-evaluated in approximately three weeks.
injuries.detail: Beekman is set for an extended absence, with his re-evaluation timeline suggesting he could remain sidelined beyond the initial three-week window. The injury further limits Washington's backcourt depth, though Beekman's absence is unlikely to have a significant impact on standard fantasy leagues.

injuries.injury: Vukcevic (hip) has been ruled out for Tuesday's game against Boston.
injuries.detail: Vukcevic has yet to suit up this season due to a left hip injury. He can be considered week-to-week until the Wizards provide an update on his progress.
